## The idea

Choose a two-voice invention, canon, or contrapuntal excerpt. The project asks
for two lines that remain independently inspectable and reproduce the source
together. Each voice needs its own events, measure references, phrase or motive
labels, and uncertainty markers.
Complete the independent-voice model in
[Lesson 47](../10-texture-and-arrangement/47-independent-voices.qmd) and the
entry-delay analysis in
[Lesson 51](../10-texture-and-arrangement/51-canon-imitation.qmd) first. The
capstone combines those concurrency decisions with the source checks from Part
9.

Polyphonic transcription adds a vertical check to the horizontal work. A note
can be correct in its own melody and still enter at the wrong moment against the
other voice. Validate each line's bar totals, then validate shared boundaries
and inspect the intervals created at every attack.

Annotate motives, imitative entries, cadences, and implied harmony. These labels
are analytical claims, so keep them beside the score without allowing them to
change playback.

## Run this

The model uses two independent event arrays over eight beats. Motive labels show
the imitative relationship, while one alignment check confirms that both voices
finish together.

```{.ruby audio=""}
use_bpm 86

upper = [
  {note: 60, start: 0.0, duration: 1.0, motive: :subject},
  {note: 62, start: 1.0, duration: 1.0, motive: :subject},
  {note: 64, start: 2.0, duration: 2.0, motive: :subject},
  {note: 67, start: 4.0, duration: 1.0, motive: :answer},
  {note: 65, start: 5.0, duration: 1.0, motive: :answer},
  {note: 64, start: 6.0, duration: 2.0, motive: :cadence}
]

lower = [
  {note: 48, start: 0.0, duration: 2.0, motive: :support},
  {note: 55, start: 2.0, duration: 1.0, motive: :subject},
  {note: 57, start: 3.0, duration: 1.0, motive: :subject},
  {note: 59, start: 4.0, duration: 2.0, motive: :subject},
  {note: 53, start: 6.0, duration: 1.0, motive: :cadence},
  {note: 48, start: 7.0, duration: 1.0, motive: :cadence}
]

define :play_events do |events, synth_name, amp, pan_position|
  use_synth synth_name
  cursor = 0.0
  events.each do |event|
    sleep event[:start] - cursor
    play event[:note],
      release: event[:duration] * 0.82,
      amp: amp,
      pan: pan_position
    cursor = event[:start]
  end
end

upper_end = upper.last[:start] + upper.last[:duration]
lower_end = lower.last[:start] + lower.last[:duration]
raise "voice alignment failure" unless upper_end == lower_end

in_thread { play_events upper, :piano, 0.75, 0.25 }
play_events lower, :pluck, 0.65, -0.25
```

The lower voice begins as support, then states a related rising subject while
the upper voice continues. Panning aids inspection without changing the score.

## Change one thing

1. Delay the lower subject events by 0.5 beats while leaving its first event
   fixed. The final alignment fails or events overlap. This distinguishes a
   local imitation edit from a legal whole-voice shift.
2. Transpose lower subject notes up twelve semitones. The motive stays
   recognisable, but voice crossing becomes likely. Listen for which line your
   ear follows after the crossing.
3. Mute either play_events call. Each remaining voice should have a coherent
   contour and rhythm. If one line sounds like scattered chord filler, revisit
   its event boundaries and source.

## Why it works

Independent arrays preserve horizontal identity. Global starts preserve
vertical alignment. Together they allow both kinds of query: what does this
voice do next, and what sounds against this attack?

Interval inspection uses pitch arithmetic. At every distinct attack time, find
the active note in each voice and subtract the lower from the upper. Reduce
with % 12 when pitch class is the concern, but keep the full interval to detect
crossing and register. Dissonance can be correct when prepared and resolved;
the report identifies places to analyse rather than banning interval classes.

Motive annotations resemble tags on events. An entry can share a subject label
while being transposed or rhythmically altered. Cadence and implied-harmony
labels describe spans, so a separate annotations array with start and duration
may be cleaner for a longer work.

Human comparison remains required. Syntax and alignment checks cannot confirm
that two independently valid lines match the printed score or recording.

## Take it further

Transcribe at least sixteen bars of two-voice polyphony. Deliver separate
voice arrays, per-bar duration checks, automatic final alignment, source
coordinates, and annotations for motives, imitative entries, cadences, and
implied harmony. Generate an interval report at every attack and explain each
flagged crossing or exposed dissonance. The target is a combined rendering that
matches the source while either voice remains readable and playable alone.
